title: Audit Log Gap via Disk Exhaustion-Induced Logger Crash -- T1070 Indicator Removal
author: WRG-11
description:
Detects deliberate disk-exhaustion attack pattern that causes audit logger crash and creates a forensic blind window.
Attack chain:
(1) Attacker (with low-privilege foothold) intentionally fills disk to >95% utilization via large file write (e.g., dd if=/dev/urandom of=/ tmp/junk bs=1M count=99999, or repeated tmpfs allocation).
(2) Audit logger (auditd, Windows EventLog, syslog, OpenSearch journald forwarder, etc.) loses ability to write new events. Depending on implementation: (a) logger crashes silently; (b) logger blocks writes (callers see EAGAIN/ENOSPC); (c) logger drops events silently. Either way, a forensic blind window opens.
(3) During the blind window, attacker executes higher-impact subsequent stages (lateral movement, credential dump, ransomware deployment) that would have been logged. Detection at SIEM is permanently lost for the duration.
(4) After completing primary objective, attacker (a) optionally restores disk via cleanup; (b) leaves the system in degraded state.
Detection logic targets the COMPOSITE pattern, not the individual signals (each is too noisy alone):
- Disk utilization >95% on a security-relevant volume (host root, /var, /var/log, log retention partition) - AND concurrent (within 5-min window) security tool exception logged (auditd OOM, syslog rotation failure, EventLog service stop) - AND audit log timestamp discontinuity > X minutes (forensic blind window candidate, configurable threshold)
Multi-signal correlation prevents false positives from legitimate disk pressure events (which usually trigger only signal 1 OR signal 2 alone, not both with timestamp gap).
Sister: defense-evasion via indicator removal (T1070 base technique) extends to T1070.001 (clear Windows event logs) and T1070.002 (clear Linux/Mac system logs); this rule is the disk- exhaustion-induced variant.
